openings.claim: A thumb-actuated captive plunger might reseat the clip; its guided head is predicted to align the impulse with the clip axis and retain moving parts.
openings.discriminator: Predicts adequate seating, without ordering performance against the spring latch. Failure to seat, loss of grip, or wiring contact defeats adequacy.
openings.probe: Proposed only: exercise orientations on a wiring surrogate; assess seating, retention, and grip.
openings.uncertainty: Available thumb force and guidance tolerance are unresolved.

openings.claim: A captive spring head held by an elastomer latch may deliver a repeatable tap; stored spring energy is predicted to reduce dependence on thumb speed.
openings.discriminator: Predicts less tap-to-tap variation than the plunger, without higher seating success. Equivalent or greater variation defeats the comparative prediction.
openings.probe: Proposed only: establish compatible latch material availability, then compare repeated strokes on a surrogate.
openings.uncertainty: Indispensable latch material and release stability are unknown; hard constraints remain in force.

lineage.reason: Adequacy relation, defeat conditions, proposed probe, uncertainty, and declared fit preserved.
Variation comparison, absence of seating superiority, defeat condition, material prerequisite, uncertainty, and declared fit preserved.

An unattached dropped weight might seat the clip through gravity-supplied impact energy, but violates no-detached-fall: successful seating cannot remove that violation. Probe parked; no overhead trial proposed. Sufficient energy and wiring contact remain unresolved.

decision: Retain D1 and D2 as synthetic proposals without confirming evidence. Reseating must maintain a secure one-hand grip: one hand operates and retains the device, no detached part falls, and contact avoids adjacent wiring. Clip geometry is hypothetical; the captive-head concept exists only as a drawing. D2 remains contingent on unknown compatible elastomer latch material; unknown resources authorize no constraint relaxation.
